diagnostic_evidence.quote: The variational particle method (\ref{djko_p2}--\ref{update_f}) has the following properties for any $n \geq 0$: (i) Discrete entropy dissipation: $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \log f^{n+1}(\bv_i^{n+1}) \leq \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \log f^n(\bv_i^{n})$.

Initialize neural network $\bu^{n+1}_\theta$ from the previously trained $\bu^{n}_\theta$. Update $\theta$ of $\bu^{n+1}_\theta$ by minimizing the JKO loss $\ell^{n+1}$ \eqref{jko_loss} using Algorithm \ref{algorithm_opt}.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims exact entropy dissipation for the proposed method. The formal entropy-dissipation result Proposition \ref{prop:added-4} applies only to the exact minimizer of the variational problem \eqref{djko_p2}. The implemented method approximates the vector field by a neural network and minimizes the loss with stochastic optimization, so entropy dissipation is not exact. Moreover, the variational problem itself is ill-posed (see ISSUE-004).

failure_location.quote: Compared to other deterministic particle methods, the proposed method enjoys exact entropy dissipation and unconditional stability

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the claim to say that the exact variational scheme is designed to be entropy dissipative, while neural-network and stochastic approximations introduce errors.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised exact entropy-dissipation guarantee is not established for the actual neural-network/SGD algorithm.
issues.title: Abstract overclaims exact entropy dissipation for the implemented neural-network method
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short qualification of the abstract claim; it does not require new mathematics, though it removes an unsupported guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We now demonstrate that \eqref{djko} indeed provides a first-order in $\tau$ approximation to \eqref{landau_homo}.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting u(1)=τ∇log f into the constraint yields ∂t f(1)=τ Q(f(1),f(1)), a rescaled Landau operator, not the Landau equation itself. The discrete JKO step is only a first-order approximation in τ, not an exact solution after time τ.

failure_location.quote: Substituting \eqref{opt_u1} into the constraint PDE in \eqref{djko} reveals that $f^{n+1} = f(1, \cdot)$ is indeed the solution of the homogeneous Landau equation \eqref{landau_homo} after one time step $\tau$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase to say that the step gives a first-order-in-τ approximation to the Landau equation.
issues.overall_effect: The prose overclaims the exactness of the one-step scheme.
issues.title: Prose overstates one JKO step as exact Landau solution
issues.why_classification: A short local rewording fixes the overstatement; the paper elsewhere correctly states first-order accuracy.

\frac{\rd}{\rd t} \log |\det \nabla_\bv T_t(\bv)| = \!-\! \int_{\R^d} \!\bigg\{ A(T_t(\bv) \!-\! T_t(\bv_*)) : \nabla\bu(t, T_t(\bv)) \!-\! (d\!-\!1) C_{\gamma} |T_t(\bv)\!-\!T_t(\bv_*)|^{\gamma}(T_t(\bv) \!-\! T_t(\bv_*)) \cdot [\bu(t, T_t(\bv)) \!-\! \bu(t, T_t(\bv_*))] \bigg\} f^n_* \rd\bv_*

issues.failure_explanation: The action only penalizes differences u(T_i)-u(T_j) along the flow. One can choose u vanishing at all particle trajectories while making its gradient ∇u arbitrarily large there. Then the action is zero, but the log-determinant term can be made arbitrarily large positive or negative, so the objective has infimum -∞. Thus the arginf in \eqref{djko_L2}, and consequently in \eqref{djko_p} and \eqref{djko_p2}, is not well-defined.

failure_location.quote: \inf_{\bu} \ \frac12 \int_0^1 \iint_{\R^{2d}} |\bu(t, T_t(\bv)) - \bu(t, T_t(\bv_*))|^2_A f^n f^n_* \rd\bv \rd\bv_* \rd t -2\tau\int_{\R^d} f^n\log|\det\nabla_\bv T_1(\bv)| \rd\bv

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a coercive regularizer on ∇u or reformulate the scheme so that the log-determinant term is controlled by the action; this requires a nontrivial change to the variational problem.
issues.overall_effect: The variational JKO scheme is ill-posed; existence of a minimizer and the entropy-dissipation guarantee based on it fail.
issues.title: Lagrangian/particle JKO variational problem is unbounded below
issues.why_classification: No complete local repair preserves the method: without controlling ∇u, the central optimization problem has no minimizer, undermining the exact entropy-dissipation and stability claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Of particular interest is the case when $d = 3$ and $\gamma = -3$, which corresponds to the Coulomb interaction

issues.failure_explanation: The double sums and particle updates run over all j including j=i. For γ<-2, e.g. Coulomb γ=-3, the kernel A(z)=C_γ|z|^{γ+2}Π(z) diverges at z=0, so A(v_i-v_i) is undefined. Thus the particle formulation and update equations are ill-defined for the paper's central Coulomb case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Exclude j=i from all particle sums, or define A(0)=0 and justify that the self-term does not affect the discretization.
issues.overall_effect: The particle method is not well-defined for Coulomb and other soft potentials with γ<-2 unless self-interaction is excluded or A(0) is suitably regularized.
issues.title: Particle sums include undefined self-interaction for Coulomb/soft potentials
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard local exclusion of self-interaction; it preserves the method and all advertised cases.

issues.failure_explanation: Multiplying the bound from Lemma \ref{sgd_lemma1} by the factor \frac{\alpha L^2 B}{2N} from Lemma \ref{sgd_lemma2} gives \frac{\alpha^3 L^2 N}{2B}(...), not \frac{\alpha^3 L^2 N}{2B^2}(...). The source drops a factor B. Consequently the step-size condition and the final bound with N/B^2 are incorrect; the correct variance term is N/B.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the algebra: the variance term becomes 6σ^2 L^2 α^2 N/B, and the step-size condition adjusts accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated convergence rate and learning-rate condition in Theorem \ref{thm_opt_conv} are incorrect.
issues.title: Algebra error in Theorem thm_opt_conv convergence bound
issues.why_classification: The error is a contained algebraic mistake in the convergence proof; the theorem can likely be salvaged with corrected constants and a weakened rate.
